powerModel.assumptions: R30 uses 4.2 peak-sun-hours, a 75% solar yield factor, 50% GEL depth of discharge, about 0.10 kWh/day for the always-on Ekrano GX and a 15 m one-way copper PV run. The use profile is UniFi plus Starlink Mini for 8 hours/day, four to six ordinary USB devices averaging about 15 W each for 4–5 hours, and one 600–1,200 W corded tool during a 2–3 hour work period. Use 3.0 kWh/day as the normal planning budget and about 4.9 kWh/day as the continuous maximum-tool case; actual intermittent tools should fall between them. The 590 W USB figure is simultaneous installed output capacity, not daily energy demand. The 3 × 490 W AIKO-A490-MCE54Mw string is 1,470 W, 104.1 Vmp, 123.3 V Voc at 25°C and about 127.37 V Voc at 10°C. One 4 mm² pair carries 14.13 A Imp / 14.88 A Isc through one 20 A common-trip two-pole cutoff; no combiner rails, active SPD or redundant PV disconnect are modeled. PV cable loss uses 0.01724 Ω·mm²/m copper resistivity at 20°C and is about 25.82 W / 1.76% over the 30 m loop. Around 24 V the array can supply roughly 60 A through the SmartSolar, but its battery branch retains Victron's 35 mm² / 100–120 A envelope because the 150/85 hardware remains capable of 85 A and the battery can backfeed a fault. Field conductor sizes consolidate to 1/0 AWG, 35 mm², 16 mm², 6 mm², 4 mm² and 1.5 mm², plus purpose-built multicore/factory leads. The 1,200 W tool is about 67.2 A DC at the conservative 19 V / 94% case; with high-power USB branches off, essential services bring the controlled SmartShunt trunk to about 72.9 A. All installed DC branches at published maximum with the tool could reach about 115.0 A, so the operating rule remains conditional. Set the Ekrano DVCC bank charge-current ceiling to 88 A, equal to Victron's preferred 0.2 C limit for 440 Ah. Tool starting surge, MultiPlus external DC protection, fault-current coordination, received terminals and hot-installation ampacity still require commissioning evidence.

A 2 ft / 0.61 m nominal piece is not automatically assigned to a 0.74 m routed lead because termination take-up, bends and service slack make it too short. batteryCablePlan.measurementRule: Use the routed centerlines only as geometry evidence. Mock up the received batteries, DIHOOL cutoff devices, external SmartShunt, Joinfworld buses and MultiPlus at full size; measure along the supported conductor path and verify terminal take-up, service slack, bend radius, lug orientation and paired-path requirements before selecting or ordering an assembly. Battery and MultiPlus posts require M8 while the purchased assemblies have 3/8 in / M10 rings, and the DIHOOL/SmartSolar devices use clamp terminals; use only approved terminations or transitions. Never trim strands, drill lugs or claim UL 1426/tinned-marine construction without received markings.

operatingRules: Keep the one AIKO 3S string on its single 4 mm² positive/negative home run to the indoor entry junction box. Route it through exactly one verified 20 A common-trip two-pole cutoff and then directly to the SmartSolar. Do not add branch connectors, comb rails, the supplied fuse links, an active SPD or a redundant disconnect to the R30 topology.

Use one corded power tool at a time from the dedicated trailing socket and keep the tool nameplate at or below about 1,200 W. Fully uncoil and inspect the lead before use; do not add a power board, daisy-chain another extension, or combine the saw with the planer, jigsaw, drill, kettle or another large AC load. Hang the lead dry beside the equipment after use.
Run tool work mainly in sunny hours. Stop tool loads around 50% state of charge; reserve the lower half of the GEL bank for longevity and essentials.

Keep the AC inverter off when no AC loads are required. Use STARLINK + UNIFI to shut down Starlink and UniFi overnight, and use ORION REMOTE H to put the Orion below 1 mA remote-off standby. The four breaker-protected ChargeIT Minis have no remote shutoff; measure their combined idle draw and open their 32 A branch breaker when long-term shutdown is needed.
Leave the Ekrano GX powered so it can retain battery history and report alarms. Let its display time out when not in use; investigate alarms locally before resetting them.

Keep both internal 120 A battery-string breakers ON in normal service only after the received DIHOOL devices pass documented DC-rating, interrupt-capacity, terminal and acceptance checks. Switch both OFF after AC loads, MultiPlus, PV and generator charging are shut down. Battery fault energy remains substantial.

If a battery or balancer alarm suggests a bad string: shut down every load and charge source, switch both string breakers OFF, verify individual battery and string voltages with a multimeter, and disconnect and insulate both leads of the diagnosed bad string. Only then may the healthy string's breaker be returned ON. Reduce the Ekrano DVCC charge-current limit from 88 A to 44 A. A single healthy 220 Ah string can still operate one ordinary power tool, but runtime and surge headroom are roughly halved: work in sun, monitor voltage and temperature, and stop immediately on excessive sag, alarm or breaker trip.
Never equalize GEL batteries. Inspect individual battery voltage, temperature, swelling, torque and corrosion monthly.

Keep all power electronics dry and away from direct salt air. Every three months, isolate the system, inspect for salt deposits or corrosion, clean/replace the alcove filter and correct any moisture source.

Treat the generator as tested backup only. Have the qualified installer verify the accepted AC-input assembly, generator neutral-earth arrangement and coordination between the input and output 30 mA devices. Keep AC-in N and AC-out N isolated; only protective earth is common, through the continuous unswitched PE chain. Do not add a permanent N–PE link in the AC box.

AC neutral and PE are not interchangeable. Neutral carries normal load return current; PE normally carries no current and remains continuously bonded for fault protection. Never switch PE, never use PE as a neutral, and never add a permanent N–PE link in the AC box—the MultiPlus ground relay manages the output bond.

Treat the 10 A shared-services breaker as a 160 W planning ceiling, not a promise of 240 W continuous expansion. The current 60 W expected / 100 W conservative load is appropriate. Before adding anything, recompute demand at 20 V, preserve the 10 A conductor limit and verify enclosure-temperature/curve margin.

Before running a high-load corded tool, switch ORION REMOTE H off and open the ChargeIT 32 A branch breaker; keep only the Ekrano and shared essential services running. Together with the one-tool 1,200 W limit, this keeps the modeled common battery-return current near 72.9 A at the conservative 19 V floor, below its 120 A envelope. Do not defeat the Ekrano DVCC 88 A system charge-current limit.
commissioning: Confirm all three panel nameplates are AIKO-A490-MCE54Mw and all four battery nameplates are Victron BAT412201104 before terminating anything. Do not silently substitute the similarly named AIKO 3P+ MCE54Dw construction.

Allocate the five retained Shirbly fixed-length 1/0 AWG red/black pairs (ten individual cables, 17 conductor-feet) only where received length, conductor markings and lug geometry match the verified route. Do not count the four returned iGreely pairs as inventory. Purchase the remaining correctly terminated red and black 1/0 AWG cable onsite in Fiji, including both MultiPlus feeds. Bench-check the DIHOOL clamps, battery M8 posts, SmartShunt M10 studs, Joinfworld studs and MultiPlus M8 posts; reject any forced bend or incompatible lug.

Separately fully charge and voltage-match the four Victron 220 Ah GEL batteries. Build two matched 24 V / 220 Ah series strings in parallel for 24 V / 440 Ah, install one balancer per string, and land each balancer alarm relay on its own Ekrano digital input.

Fit exactly the two selected non-polarized DIHOOL 120 A battery-string breakers plus the SmartSolar 120 A cutoff in the verified HT-8 battery-adjacent enclosure. Confirm received DC markings, interrupt rating, terminal capacity and torque. Wall-mount the four-stud main buses outside all enclosures with their supplied covers installed; leave the adjacent IP65 SmartShunt uncovered. Route both battery negatives only to SmartShunt BATTERY MINUS and SmartShunt SYSTEM MINUS to the main negative bus. Build the approved main-positive lug stacks with specified torque and adequate thread engagement, and document the installed conductor order.

With modules covered, connect the three AIKO modules in one 3S string using only mutually compatible original connectors. Uncover and measure about 123.3 V Voc at 25°C; confirm polarity, labels and isolation before landing the single 4 mm² positive/negative home-run pair. Confirm the 127.37 V modeled cold Voc remains within both the selected cutoff and SmartSolar limits, then confirm the SmartSolar's protected battery branch before closing the PV cutoff.

Install exactly one of the purchased 20 A common-trip two-pole CHTAIXI devices as the 3S-array cutoff only after received-marking, polarity, cold-Voc, interrupt-rating, torque and local-acceptance checks. Keep the second 20 A unit uninstalled as a labeled spare or return it; keep the older 32 A pair out of the design and return it.

Program MultiPlus and SmartSolar for the exact Victron GEL label and current manual; planning values are 28.2 V absorption, 27.2 V float and equalization disabled. Install the temperature sensor supplied with the 24 V MultiPlus on Battery 1's negative terminal. In Ekrano DVCC, select the SmartShunt for Shared Voltage Sense and Shared Current Sense, select the MultiPlus sensor for Shared Temperature Sense, and set the system-wide charge-current limit to 88 A with both strings healthy. Do not add a Smart Battery Sense unless this wired sensing path is later removed or proves unusable.

Keep the returned SCC950400300 / MC4 WireBox out of project inventory and confirm its $38.85 refund settles by 2 Sep 2026. Obtain SCC950400210 WireBox-XL Tr for the purchased SmartSolar 150/85-Tr VE.Can, verify both part-number labels and install per Victron's quick guide.
Set the MultiPlus to 230 V / 50 Hz with a 10 A AC input-current limit for the G3200P; verify generator acceptance before enabling unattended charging.

With the 24 V bank isolated, install the accepted verified-fit HT-8 battery/MPPT cutoff enclosure and select the larger secondary-services enclosure from the current 600 × 640 × 240 mm routed envelope. Mount both secondary buses against its rear backplate about one-third of the way up, and place the six-gang panel and UniFi converter against the rear top edge with every post facing down. Keep the one bottom gland row unobstructed and route every unrelated cable around—never in front of—mounted equipment. Keep the MultiPlus, SmartSolar, Orion and secondary enclosure on the common lower datum; mount the compact single-breaker PV junction box immediately above the shared service penetration, with both AC cable breakouts below the inverter. Preserve breaker access, bends, guarded terminals, ventilation, sealing, cable entries and shortest-practical 1/0 AWG battery leads.

Power the Ekrano directly from the protected 24 V bus with its supplied 3.15 A slow-blow fused lead, with negative on the system side of the SmartShunt. Never power it from MultiPlus AC-out or from the voltage-controlled DC-load branch.

Connect the MultiPlus by Victron RJ45 UTP/VE.Bus, SmartSolar and SmartShunt by separate VE.Direct cables, both balancer alarm relays to separate Ekrano digital inputs, and Ekrano Ethernet to the UniFi Express LAN port. Confirm all three Victron devices, SmartShunt battery state, battery temperature, SVS/SCS/STS sources and both balancer alarms appear locally.

Register the Ekrano in VRM over UniFi/Starlink, enable HTTPS and two-factor authentication on administrator accounts, configure useful battery/temperature/offline alarms, set a connection-appropriate log interval, and test both local operation without internet and remote recovery after reconnect.
Set the Ekrano display auto-off timer and adaptive brightness, record the VRM Portal ID and access recovery details off-site, and export configuration backups before departure.
Torque to each manufacturer specification; re-torque after the first week and mark fasteners with witness paint.

Keep both purchased Mollom HT-8 units out of the installed AC assembly. Install the separately tracked second HT-8 as the verified-fit R30 three-device battery/MPPT cutoff enclosure; retain the first as an owned spare. The two purchased DIHOOL 10 A ground-fault/surge units are assigned to AC-in and AC-out, but both remain commissioning holds until exact 10 A, 30 mA Type A, SPD classification, L/N/PE arrangement, interrupt rating, 230 V / 50 Hz suitability and qualified-installer acceptance are confirmed. Purchase-fade state must not be interpreted as electrical approval. No unselected replacement AC-enclosure allowance remains in the BOM; add only the actual AC enclosure after its separate fit check.

Route four separate three-core cables through the AC enclosure: generator → input LINE, input LOAD → MultiPlus AC-in, MultiPlus AC-out-1 → output LINE, and output LOAD → Type I trailing socket. Keep the two neutrals segregated. Daisy-chain PE only through dedicated unswitched PE pass-through terminals rated for the exact conductor count: generator → input protector → MultiPlus chassis/PE → output protector → socket, with the main PE bond joined at the input PE node. If any received terminal cannot do this, use a larger enclosure and approved PE terminal block.

Cut the purchased six-gang panel opening at the accepted secondary-services enclosure face/cover location from the verified layout. Label the vertical rockers, top to bottom: STARLINK + UNIFI; OUTDOOR LIGHT; ORION REMOTE H; SPARE; SPARE; SPARE. Gasket the perimeter, insulate every rear terminal and verify the protected daisy-chain conductors. Switch 3 carries only the Orion H-pin control signal; L is unused and USB charging current bypasses the switch panel.

Secure two genuine WAGO 221-413 connectors in proper carriers inside the secondary-services enclosure. The first splits the purchased CHTAIXI 10 A shared-services positive branch between the six-gang common feed and remote room-switch run. The second splits the STARLINK + UNIFI positive switch output between the Starlink bulkhead jack and dedicated UniFi converter. Do not add modeled negative-return split devices: land the nine graph connections directly on the seven-position secondary negative bus, retain the terminal-count warning, and select any necessary listed splitter arrangement onsite. Connect Starlink Ethernet directly to the UniFi Express WAN port and bench-test at least ten simultaneous Starlink/UniFi power cycles.

Use QHLightlux B0F1V59NXC 3000 K fixtures for both locations. Suspend the indoor unit from a short dry bracket with its lens down; mount the outdoor unit under an eave with 316 stainless fasteners and sealed bedding. Put two 3 A silicon rectifier diodes in series with each switched positive branch. Route one protected positive from the secondary-services enclosure to one pole of the IP66 DPST switch beside the opposite doorway, one switched positive onward to the indoor fixture, and one direct unswitched negative from the secondary negative bus to the fixture. Dress all three long conductors along the ceiling, cap the unused pole and verify the received contact diagram before energizing.

Bench-test the Starlink Mini from the 24 V branch through its complete OEM 15 m cable: verify center-positive polarity at the bulkhead jack, cold-start it at low battery voltage, and confirm STARLINK + UNIFI simultaneously removes Starlink and UniFi without interrupting the independently switched USB or lights.

Run the largest permitted 1,200 W tool alone for 30 minutes in warm conditions with the 5 m lead fully uncoiled while monitoring inverter, lead, plug/socket, cable and terminal temperature; post the one-page operating rules and breaker map beside the equipment.

Continuity-test the complete AC PE chain with each protection device ON and OFF. Prove low-resistance continuity from generator earth and the main PE bond to MultiPlus chassis and the Type I socket, prove no input-neutral/output-neutral cross-connection, and test the MultiPlus ground-relay behavior in inverter and generator/bypass modes before energizing the socket.

Build the secondary-services rail with exactly three branch positions: purchased CHTAIXI B09H4W5HSW 10 A shared services, purchased 32 A Orion input and purchased 32 A ChargeIT. Do not add a separate 80 A incomer. Verify the received B10 12–110 VDC/polarity/curve/6 kA/terminal/torque markings and bound battery prospective fault current before energizing it. The direct secondary feeder remains a separate hold until source-side overcurrent protection, its ampacity and both 100 A bus interfaces are accepted.

No insulated secondary-enclosure feed-through studs are purchased. Route one held positive feeder and one negative feeder through ordinary strain-relieved glands unless a stud pair is later selected and electrically and mechanically verified. Verify both purchased 32 A breakers, their 24 V conductors and every downstream terminal before energizing. The verified Orion output limiter enables its downstream socket routes, but retain the graph verifier's separate limitation until the published short-circuit envelope, harness ampacity and fault-clearing behavior are coordinated.

Use the canonical graph as the wiring authority: every physical device and conductor in the detailed diagram is the same object rendered in 3D. Treat its programmatic per-supply current-protection traversal as fail-closed evidence: resolve missing source/channel/return metadata, inadequate ratings, bypasses and incomplete fault-clearing evidence before commissioning. Resolve graph validation or A* routing failures in code; do not add hand-positioned glands, routing exceptions or undocumented wires.

Before commissioning the MultiPlus DC branch, follow the exact 24/3000/70 manual: select a resettable external DC breaker with a manufacturer-accepted trip characteristic and adequate interrupt rating, use at least the specified 50 mm² copper for a 0–5 m run (or the final engineer-sized conductor), and re-check the 250 A buses and two 120 A string-breaker architecture. Do not rely on MultiPlus internal electronic protection to protect the field cable.

Use 4 mm² PV cable continuously from the single AIKO 3S string through the one 20 A two-pole cutoff to the SmartSolar. There is no combined-array segment: do not install the old comb rails, supplied 32 A fuse links, SPD or redundant disconnect. Confirm conductor markings, connector compatibility, gland seals, terminal range and torque before uncovering the array.

Measure every active device during bench commissioning: record Starlink average/peak, UniFi converter input and temperature, both switch-indicator draws, Coolgear 145 W idle draw, and actual ChargeIT idle draw. Compare results with the device-power table and lower operating limits if measured values exceed it.

Verify the SmartShunt SYSTEM MINUS-to-main-negative-bus trunk under the controlled operating envelope before commissioning. Confirm the actual 1/0 conductor, insulation, support, lugs and terminations sustain the modeled 120 A envelope; enforce one tool at or below 1,200 W, ORION REMOTE H off and the ChargeIT breaker open during heavy tool use, and the Ekrano DVCC charge-current limit at 88 A. The controlled discharge budget is about 72.9 A, but every installed DC branch at maximum could reach about 115.0 A if the load-shedding rule is ignored. Test and record SmartShunt current and temperature during the 30-minute tool run. Fault/OCP coordination remains a separate hold; do not infer cable ampacity from the SmartShunt's 500 A body rating.
